Jak se nazývá nádobka na cukr podávaný například ke kávě?
Jak se nazývá pokrývka hlavy, která na rozdíl od klobouku obvykle nemá okraj po celém obvodu?
Jak říkáme velkému kusu měkké tkaniny, kterým se přikryjeme například při odpočinku na pohovce?
Jak se nazývá pohyblivé schodiště, kterým se svezeme mezi patry obchodního domu?
Jak se nazývá drobná nádoba, která při pečení dá těstu určitý tvar?
Jak se hovorově nazývají nepromokavé vysoké boty vhodné do bláta a louží?
Jakou pomůckou s řadou zubů si rozčesáváme vlasy?
Jak se běžně nazývá venkovský obytný dům užívaný například k víkendové rekreaci?
Jak se nazývá krátké veřejné oznámení, jímž někdo například nabízí práci nebo prodává věc?
Jak se nazývá mléčný výrobek, který vzniká kvašením mléka pomocí bakteriálních kultur?
Jakým malým předmětem obvykle odemykáme mechanický zámek dveří?
Jak se nazývá část košile nebo kabátu, která lemuje krk?
Jak se nazývá tradiční mycí prostředek vznikající reakcí tuků se zásadou?
Jakým drobným zdravotnickým prostředkem s lepicími okraji zakryjeme malé poranění kůže?
Jak se nazývá prosklený otvor ve stěně, kterým do místnosti proniká denní světlo?
Jak se nazývá malé pouzdro, v němž nosíme bankovky, mince či platební karty?
Jaký kus oděvu chrání ruce například před zimou a může mít podobu palčáků?
Jak se nazývá kosmetický přípravek, který se kartáčkem nanáší na řasy, aby je ztmavil a zvýraznil?
Jak se nazývá úklidová pomůcka s dlouhou násadou a štětinami pro zametání podlahy?
Jak se nazývá dlouhý pruh látky, který si v zimě omotáme kolem krku?
Jak se nazývá obvykle plochá nádoba, ze které jíme hlavní jídlo?
Jak se nazývá textilie rozprostřená přes jídelní stůl, která jej zdobí a chrání?
Kterou součástí příboru s několika hroty napichujeme sousta?
Jak se nazývá malá digitální kamera připojená k počítači nebo vestavěná do notebooku, běžně používaná při videohovorech?
Jak se nazývá předmět s hladkou odraznou plochou, ve kterém vidíme vlastní obraz?
Jak se nazývá volný domácí plášť, který si často oblékáme po koupeli?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: An aquarium (pl.: aquariums or aquaria) is a vivarium of any size having at least one transparent side in which aquatic plants or animals are kept and displayed. Fishkeepers use aquaria to keep fish, invertebrates, amphibians, aquatic reptiles, such as turtles, and aquatic plants. The term aquarium, coined by English naturalist Philip Henry Gosse, combines the Latin root aqua, meaning "water," with the suffix -arium, meaning "a place for relating to or connected with."[1]

In modern usage, a cottage is usually a modest, often cosy dwelling, typically in a rural or semi-rural location and not necessarily in England. The cottage orné, often quite large and grand residences built by the nobility, dates back to a movement of "rustic" stylised cottages of the late 18th and early 19th century during the Romantic movement.

entries.claim: Jak se nazývá tradiční mycí prostředek vznikající reakcí tuků se zásadou?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage:
Soap is a salt of a fatty acid (sometimes other carboxylic acids) used for cleaning and lubricating products as well as other applications.[1] In a domestic setting, soaps, specifically "toilet soaps", are surfactants typically used for washing, bathing, and other types of housekeeping. In industrial settings, soaps are used as thickeners, components of some lubricants, emulsifiers, and catalysts.

The production of toilet soaps usually entails the saponification of triglycerides, which are vegetable or animal oils and fats. An alkaline solution (often lye) induces saponification whereby the triglyceride fats first hydrolyze into salts of fatty acids. Glycerol (glycerin) is then liberated. The glycerin is sometimes left in the soap product as a softening agent, making the soap itself softer, although it is occasionally separated.[14][15] The addition of glycerol and the processing of this soap produces glycerin soap.

Normally in one of three forms—liquid, powder, or cream—the modern mascara product has various formulas; however, most contain the same basic components of pigments, oils, waxes, and preservatives. evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: A plate is a broad, mainly flat vessel on which food can be served.[1] A plate can also be used for ceremonial or decorative purposes. Most plates are circular, but they may be any shape, or made of any water, or shatter resistant material. Generally plates are raised round the edges, either by a curving up, or a wider lip or raised portion. Vessels with no lip, especially if they have a more rounded profile, are likely to be considered as bowls or dishes, as are very large vessels with a plate shape. Plates are dishware, and tableware. Plates in wood, pottery and metal go back into antiquity in many cultures.

Some tablecloths are designed as part of an overall table setting, with coordinating napkins, placemats, or other decorative pieces. Special kinds of tablecloth include "runners" which overhang the table at two ends only and "table protectors" which provide a padded layer under a normal tablecloth.

entries.claim: Jak se nazývá předmět s hladkou odraznou plochou, ve kterém vidíme vlastní obraz?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: A mirror, also known as a looking glass, is an object that reflects an image. Light that bounces off a mirror forms an image of whatever is in front of it, which is then focused through the lens of the eye or a camera. Mirrors reverse the direction of light at an angle equal to its incidence. This allows the viewer to see themselves or objects behind them, or even objects that are at an angle from them but out of their field of view, such as around a corner. Natural mirrors have existed since prehistoric times, such as the surface of water, but people have been manufacturing mirrors out of a variety of materials for thousands of years, like stone, metals, and glass. In modern mirrors, metals like silver or aluminium are often used due to their high reflectivity, applied as a thin coating on glass because of its naturally smooth and hard surface.

evidence.passage: An aquarium (pl.: aquariums or aquaria) is a vivarium of any size having at least one transparent side in which aquatic plants or animals are kept and displayed. Fishkeepers use aquaria to keep fish, invertebrates, amphibians, aquatic reptiles, such as turtles, and aquatic plants. The term aquarium, coined by English naturalist Philip Henry Gosse, combines the Latin root aqua, meaning "water," with the suffix -arium, meaning "a place for relating to or connected with."[1]

entries.claim: Jak se běžně nazývá venkovský obytný dům užívaný například k víkendové rekreaci?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: A cottage during England's feudal period was the holding by a cottager (known as a cotter or bordar) of a small house with enough garden to feed a family and in return for the cottage, the cottager had to provide some form of service to the manorial lord.[1] However, in time cottage just became the general term for a small house. In modern usage, a cottage is usually a modest, often cosy dwelling, typically in a rural or semi-rural location and not necessarily in England. The cottage orné, often quite large and grand residences built by the nobility, dates back to a movement of "rustic" stylised cottages of the late 18th and early 19th century during the Romantic movement.

entries.claim: Jak se nazývá tradiční mycí prostředek vznikající reakcí tuků se zásadou?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage:
Soap is a salt of a fatty acid (sometimes other carboxylic acids) used for cleaning and lubricating products as well as other applications.[1] In a domestic setting, soaps, specifically "toilet soaps", are surfactants typically used for washing, bathing, and other types of housekeeping. In industrial settings, soaps are used as thickeners, components of some lubricants, emulsifiers, and catalysts.

The production of toilet soaps usually entails the saponification of triglycerides, which are vegetable or animal oils and fats. An alkaline solution (often lye) induces saponification whereby the triglyceride fats first hydrolyze into salts of fatty acids. Glycerol (glycerin) is then liberated. The glycerin is sometimes left in the soap product as a softening agent, making the soap itself softer, although it is occasionally separated.[14][15] The addition of glycerol and the processing of this soap produces glycerin soap.

The glycerin is sometimes left in the soap product as a softening agent, making the soap itself softer, although it is occasionally separated.[14][15] The addition of glycerol and the processing of this soap produces glycerin soap.

entries.claim: Jak se nazývá obvykle plochá nádoba, ze které jíme hlavní jídlo?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: A plate is a broad, mainly flat vessel on which food can be served.[1] A plate can also be used for ceremonial or decorative purposes. Most plates are circular, but they may be any shape, or made of any water, or shatter resistant material. Generally plates are raised round the edges, either by a curving up, or a wider lip or raised portion. Vessels with no lip, especially if they have a more rounded profile, are likely to be considered as bowls or dishes, as are very large vessels with a plate shape. Plates are dishware, and tableware. Plates in wood, pottery and metal go back into antiquity in many cultures.

evidence.passage: A tablecloth is a cloth used to cover a table. Some are mainly ornamental coverings, which may also help protect the table from scratches and stains. Other tablecloths are designed to be spread on a dining table before laying out tableware and food. Some tablecloths are designed as part of an overall table setting, with coordinating napkins, placemats, or other decorative pieces. Special kinds of tablecloth include "runners" which overhang the table at two ends only and "table protectors" which provide a padded layer under a normal tablecloth.

entries.claim: Jak se nazývá předmět s hladkou odraznou plochou, ve kterém vidíme vlastní obraz?

evidence.sourceQuality: Wikipedia public secondary encyclopedia; not primary institutional evidence
evidence.passage: A mirror, also known as a looking glass, is an object that reflects an image. Light that bounces off a mirror forms an image of whatever is in front of it, which is then focused through the lens of the eye or a camera. Mirrors reverse the direction of light at an angle equal to its incidence. This allows the viewer to see themselves or objects behind them, or even objects that are at an angle from them but out of their field of view, such as around a corner. Natural mirrors have existed since prehistoric times, such as the surface of water, but people have been manufacturing mirrors out of a variety of materials for thousands of years, like stone, metals, and glass. In modern mirrors, metals like silver or aluminium are often used due to their high reflectivity, applied as a thin coating on glass because of its naturally smooth and hard surface.

evidence.passage: A mirror, also known as a looking glass, is an object that reflects an image. Light that bounces off a mirror forms an image of whatever is in front of it, which is then focused through the lens of the eye or a camera. Mirrors reverse the direction of light at an angle equal to its incidence. This allows the viewer to see themselves or objects behind them, or even objects that are at an angle from them but out of their field of view, such as around a corner. Natural mirrors have existed since prehistoric times, such as the surface of water, but people have been manufacturing mirrors out of a variety of materials for thousands of years, like stone, metals, and glass. In modern mirrors, metals like silver or aluminium are often used due to their high reflectivity, applied as a thin coating on glass because of its naturally smooth and hard surface.
